contact_edits.before: Roy's adaptation veers between neat versifying and prosaic bathos. As a director, he confronts a fearsome task with limited resources: The choreography (by Hari Krishnan) is more dutiful than beguiling, though Itai Erdal's lighting can be magical, especially when summoning a slow dawn. The cast is mixed, in both background and accomplishment. In the two leading roles, Anita Majumdar and Sanjay Talwar are, ethnicity notwithstanding, miscast. Talwar, a fine actor of gawks and geeks, makes the king's puzzled conscientiousness endearing sympathetic; but he is not a natural authority figure in a dramatic world that calls out for it. Majumdar, by contrast, is too worldly and controlled for Sakuntala's initial innocence. They both give us the outlines of their predicaments, but not the texture. The other players do a lot of doubling, some of it confusing. Indian audiences may know the story by heart; the rest of us need to have it told as well as decorated. It feels like a masterpiece, but we have to take a lot on trust. - Shakuntala runs until Feb. 15. Call 416-973-4000 for more information.
